rules.text: If Branch B (Direct) claims a 'hyperintense' or 'bright' lesion but the query image visually lacks a distinct, high-contrast bright mass compared to the reference images, trust A (Agent).

If Branch B (Direct) identifies a 'dark' or 'elongated' lesion in the white matter that appears visually consistent with normal sulcal or ventricular structures in the reference images, trust A (Agent).
If Branch A (Agent) explicitly cites 'normal allowed variations' or 'refutation' of defect-like features in its rationale, trust A (Agent).

If Branch A (Agent) claims a 'focal hyperintense lesion' or 'ring-enhancing lesion' but the query image appears structurally symmetrical and lacks a distinct bright or ring-shaped anomaly compared to references, trust B (Direct).
If Branch A (Agent) identifies a lesion in the 'periventricular white matter' that is not visually distinguishable from normal tissue texture in the reference images, trust B (Direct).
The brain tissue is centrally located within the image frame, surrounded by a black background.
The brain cross-section exhibits a continuous, roughly oval or circular outer boundary.
The image consists of a grayscale palette (black background, gray/white tissue) with no other colors.
The brain tissue displays a granular, heterogeneous texture with visible internal structures.
Do not flag mild asymmetry in lateral ventricle size or shape as a tumor anomaly.
Ignore subtle periventricular hyperintensities or signal variations that lack distinct mass effect or borders.
Do not classify global image blurriness, noise, or low contrast as structural brain anomalies.
